repos.description: A Claude Code skill that reverse-engineers any animation frame by frame, then proves the copy moves the same.
repos.mechanism: Record a reference (site, recording, mp4, gif, Lottie) in headless Chromium on a virtual clock at fixed viewport/fps; reduce it to a spec (one row per element per property: start, duration, from-to, easing, stagger); rebuild in the project's own stack; film the copy identically and compare.

techniques: Record -> spec -> build -> verify -> repeat, usually 2-5 rounds; after 5 rounds list remaining mismatches with reasons, do not claim done.

Two match levels stated up front: 'moves the same' = trigger, order, stagger, timing within 80 ms, easing family, distance; 'pixel-perfect' = all above plus fonts/sizes/colours/spacing/assets and <=2% mean pixel mismatch.
Fit easing/springs from tracked data (overshoot + settle time); do not guess them.
Virtual clock + seeded random for capture so two captures are byte-identical; for unreproducible particles compare blurred mismatch (density/colour/motion), not dot-by-dot.
Replay the same pointer path on original and copy; side-by-side reference/clone/diff sheets, activity curves and timing error per element every round.

repos.description: Universal motion design principles for AI agents - timing, easing, choreography, and Disney animation principles adapted for UI.
repos.mechanism: Philosophy-first, implementation-agnostic skill. 8-step checklist (emotion -> personality -> property -> duration -> easing -> hero/staging -> secondary/ambient -> 1/3 rules), 4 motion-personality archetypes, Disney 12 principles adapted for UI. No renderer; hands off once to Creator MCP for MP4/GIF/Lottie export.
repos.not_when: Long-form film / narrative video (no render, no timing grid, no review loop); photoreal 3D or math animation.
techniques: 8-step checklist before any code; every animation has 3 layers: primary, secondary, ambient (flat = missing layers).

One personality per project: Playful 150-300ms, ease-out-back, 10-20% overshoot; Premium 350-600ms, cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), 0% overshoot; Corporate 200-400ms, cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), 0-3%; Energetic 100-250ms, ease-out-expo, 15-30%. Brand = 1 signature easing (80% of animations) + 3 durations + 1 entrance pattern.

Duration table: tooltip 80-120ms, button 120-180ms, card 200-350ms, modal 300-400ms, page 400-600ms, dramatic reveal 600-1200ms; distance scaling 100px=base, 200px=1.3x, 400px=1.6x, full screen=1.8-2.0x. Entrances 30-50% longer than exits (exit = 65-75% of entrance).
Latency caps: hover <100ms, press <150ms, release/settle 200-300ms, error shake 300-400ms (2-3 oscillations, +-10-15px, 0% overshoot).
Stagger: micro 20-40ms, standard 50-100ms, dramatic 100-200ms; total stagger <500ms; direction top-to-bottom, L-to-R, centre-out, reverse on exits.

Material easing: rigid 1.2x/0% overshoot, elastic 0.8x/15-25%, fluid 1.5x/5%, paper 1.0x/3-5%, gas 2.0x/0%. Springs: standard stiffness 250-350 / damping 18-24; bouncy 150-250 / 10-15; damping ratio <1 oscillates, =1 fastest no-oscillation, >1 slow settle.
Property budget: 1 property = direct, 2 = polished, 3+ = potentially overwhelming; map goal to primary property (entrance=position, emphasis=scale, error=position shake, success=scale pop).

repos.description: Cinematic launch films and motion design from code, directed by your coding agent.
repos.mechanism: Director skill for launch films (15-45s) and update videos (15-23s). Pipeline Steps 0-11, each writes a file and ends at a runnable gate: BRIEF.md -> dealt direction (deck.py, 3 directions from 35) -> script checked by copy-check.py -> brand/type -> licensed music found and analysed (music.mjs, track.py) -> beat sheet/timeline on the music's bars (pick.py draws devices) -> build from tested primitives -> look/forensics/grammar checks -> sound cast/score mastered to -14 LUFS -> motion-blurred master -> contact-sheet + critic review -> delivery. Engines: Remotion (React) default or HyperFrames (HTML/GSAP).
repos.not_when: Short doodle/art/explainer films, single-shot loops, or low-budget runs - a cinetic run costs ~3x the time/tokens of the baseline; not for photoreal/organic motion.
techniques: Copy first, before any picture: script must say what the product is by 3s, one thing it does per line, name + what to do; 2-7 plain words per line; copy-check.py fails vague words, slogans, keyword piles, lines >7 words, two lines on screen at once, 'Introducing...', eyebrow/kicker labels, fake metrics/lorem ipsum.
Direction is dealt, not improvised: deck.py --brief ... --options 3 gives 3 complete directions; agent writes one idea sentence each, keeps the one a competitor could not claim.

Device book as a draw, not a menu: 466 devices in 25 families + 724 entries in techniques.json; pick.py draws ~1 device per beat, in format order, with a variety rule (one family cannot fill a film), weighted to house workhorses and film energy, a different text animation per line; seed printed so a plan reproduces.

Velocity handoff as the default cut: outgoing shot accelerates and is cut on its fastest frame; incoming opens moving the same way at 0.5-1.5x that speed and decelerates to rest; every cut hands over a carrier (velocity, scale direction, shape or position). Numbers: exit ease-in 4-29f, entry 20-60f settling, cut speeds 15-200 px/f at 1080p; sound on the cut within +-30ms of the beat. Avoid cutting between two parked frames or into an opposite-direction move.

One grid for everything: b(bar, beat, 16ths) helper maps every frame number to the track's measured bars, so picture, cue export and audits cannot drift. Sounds are never placed by hand: export-cues.ts computes contact frames of springs, settle frames of arrivals and velocity peaks of launches from the same constants the acts animate with.

Look floors + forensics as gates: look-audit.py fails a render under the floors (camera or ground moving through most of the body, two planes at different rates, carried seams, a designed moment every 3s, a light event in every act, scale changes across cuts); forensics.py fails motion that snaps, freezes, settles too fast or stops dead; grammar-score.mjs scores against house grammar.

Sound restraint: licensed human-made instrumental track only (no generated music); one soft sound per line of text, near-silence while it is read, one big hit for the one reveal; at most 2 pitched effects in any 4s.

Templates are floors: 7 templates (update 15-23s, ui-walkthrough 25-40s, capability-reel 15-25s, camera-teaser 20-25s, prompt-run 18-20s, social-ad 15s, type-explainer 20-30s); social versions are re-laid out from the same timeline, never cropped.

repos.description: A community-maintained Python framework for creating mathematical animations.
repos.mechanism: Three concepts - Mobject (displayable object, mostly vector VMobject), Animation (interpolation between two states), Scene (construct() orchestrates). Input is a Python Scene class; self.play(Animation) renders it, CLI manim encodes MP4 via Cairo/ffmpeg. Output is deterministic video, not an interactive page.
repos.not_when: Product UI, photoreal/3D, characters, real-time or HTML seek(t) loops, short social loops.
techniques: Identity continuity: keep the same object across stages with Transform(square, circle) / Create / FadeOut, instead of title-card sequences - the audience can point to how state N became N+1.
Animation = interpolation: every animation interpolates start->end (opacity, angle, position). Name run_time and rate_func explicitly per play(); do not rely on a global default ease.
.animate chaining: any setter is animatable - square.animate.set_fill(WHITE).shift(UP).rotate(PI/3) in one play() - one causal change per beat.
Relational placement: move_to(), next_to(), align_to() relative to origin/other objects, not absolute pixels; origin is screen centre, up/right positive.
Live-updating plots: Axes/FunctionGraph/ValueTracker + always_redraw - the analogue of renderAt(t): derive the drawing from a single time/value parameter.
Cheap stills first: manim -s renders final frame only, -n <k> skips to the k-th animation, -ql low-quality preview, -p preview.

repos.description: Three.quarks is a general purpose particle system / VFX engine for three.js
repos.mechanism: ParticleSystem (data spec) + BatchedRenderer (one renderer manages all systems, minimises draw calls). Particles are defined by emitter shape + behaviours over lifetime + material, updated per frame (batchRenderer.update(delta)), rendered as billboard/stretched-billboard/mesh/trail. Effects can be authored in a visual editor and loaded from JSON.
repos.not_when: Canvas2D-only, 2D type, math diagrams, no three.js, or deterministic frame export without a seek adapter.
techniques: Particle spec as numbers: duration, looping, startLife: IntervalValue(1,2), startSpeed: ConstantValue(5), startSize: IntervalValue(0.1,0.3), startColor, maxParticle: 100, emissionOverTime: ConstantValue(20) - no adjectives, every value is a range or constant.

Emitter shapes carry identity: Point/Sphere/Hemisphere/Cone/Circle/MeshSurface/Grid - emit from a model surface or a structured grid, not a random cloud; particles must serve a recognisable silhouette.

Behaviours over lifetime: Color/Size/Rotation over life, force fields, orbital motion, texture animation, sub-emitters, PiecewiseBezier size curves - define the whole life curve up front, not per-frame tweaks.
Batched rendering: one BatchedRenderer, shared shader builds per batch kind; trail = ribbon behind particle, stretched billboard = velocity-aligned sprite.
JSON VFX library: QuarksLoader.load('effects/explosion.json'), clone() for multiple instances, setAutoDestroy(true), play() - reusable, versioned effects instead of one-off code.
Determinism warning: quarks is delta-driven (update(delta)), so a frame-accurate renderAt(t) export needs reset + deterministic stepping from absolute time; do not assume seek works out of the box.
Finish: sprite sheets with frame blending, alpha test, soft particles (depth pre-pass on WebGL, automatic on WebGPU), configurable blending.

repos.call_how: npm install @react-three/postprocessing; import {Bloom, DepthOfField, EffectComposer, Noise, Vignette} from '@react-three/postprocessing' inside <Canvas>.
repos.mechanism: Declarative React wrapper around pmndrs/postprocessing. <EffectComposer> collects child effects into one merged EffectPass (fewer render ops than chained passes, each effect its own blend function), single-triangle fullscreen passes, WebGL2 MSAA by default, gamma correction out of the box.
repos.not_when: Canvas2D, Manim, Blender, plain HTML, no React/R3F, or when the finish would hide a geometric/contact error.
techniques: Effect chain as a list, order matters: <EffectComposer><DepthOfField/><Bloom/><Noise/><Vignette/></EffectComposer> - one pass, not one render per effect.

Starting numbers from the README example (treat as starting values, verify per shot): DoF focusDistance 0, focalLength 0.02, bokehScale 2, height 480; Bloom luminanceThreshold 0, luminanceSmoothing 0.9, height 300; Noise opacity 0.02; Vignette offset 0.1, darkness 1.1.
Text/UI after DoF: never let depth-of-field or blur eat text - draw UI on its own layer after the DoF pass.
Grain cap: Noise opacity 0.02 matches grain <=0.02 rule; heavier grain + JPEG-style double compression degrades fast.
MSAA by default: crisp edges without jagged aliasing; do not add a second AA pass.
Each effect chooses its own blend function - do not force one global blend mode on the whole chain.

Strip before delivery: the pane is a tuning tool, never part of the film; remove it (or gate it behind a debug flag) in the exported HTML.

repos.call_how: CLI effectcraft-cli ..., MCP server, or JSON control channel (effectcraft --control 9877); docs docs/agents.md, docs/control-protocol.md.
repos.description: Open-source motion graphics and compositing tool written from scratch in pure Rust.
repos.mechanism: After-Effects-like compositor: compositions of layers (solids, shapes, text, footage, nested comps, nulls, cameras, lights), animated by keyframes, stacked with 308 effects and 9 layer styles, rendered via a Render Queue. Projects are versioned JSON (.ecproj); engine commands are exposed via CLI, JSON control channel and MCP; all codecs are pure Rust, no FFmpeg inside.
repos.not_when: Production client work (README: alpha, ~91% of tracked features, ~45% to production-ready); when the route is single-HTML Canvas2D / Remotion / Blender; no Rust install available.
techniques: Project as versioned, diffable JSON - extend production-project.json to a layer/keyframe schema (comp, layer, property, keyframes) an agent can edit textually and diff.

Keyframe model per property - linear / Bezier / hold / auto / continuous-Bezier, roving keys, Easy Ease, Graph Editor with value + speed graphs. Rule: every animated property declares interpolation type, not just values.
Expressions as closed-form JS - wiggle, loopOut, thisComp.layer('...'); maps directly to renderAt(t) pure-function rule, no per-frame state.

Effects taxonomy as a checklist, not a menu - 308 effects in blur/sharpen, colour, distort, generate, keying, matte, noise/grain, perspective, simulation (Particle Emitter 3D, Shatter, Caustics), stylize, time, audio, transitions; 38 blend modes, motion blur, track mattes. Use to name the one VFX pass needed, not to pile effects on.

Render Queue / Output Modules - H.264 MP4, ProRes MOV (Proxy-4444 XQ, alpha), HEVC Main/Main 10, AV1, WebM VP9/AV1 + Opus, PNG/JPEG/TIFF/EXR sequences, GIF, WAV/AIFF; templates + post-render actions. Rule: encode spec is chosen per deliverable, recorded in the brief.

Agent interface pattern - one-shot CLI with JSON output, e.g. effectcraft-cli set Main '#1' transform/position '[100,360]' --time 0 main.ecproj --save, render --comp Main --out main.mp4; MCP effectcraft-cli mcp over stdio.

repos.call_how: HTTPS GET, e.g. https://api.openverse.org/v1/audio/?q=whoosh&license=cc0&page_size=5; Python requests / curl; no key anonymous.
repos.description: Search engine for openly licensed images (800M+) and audio (~5.2M) from Flickr, Wikimedia, Freesound, Jamendo and others, with licence + attribution metadata per item.
repos.mechanism: GET /v1/audio/?q=... and /v1/images/?q=...; each result returns title, creator, license, license_url, direct file url, foreign_landing_url, duration (audio, ms), and a ready-made attribution string. Anonymous, no key; registered clients get higher limits via /v1/auth_tokens/register/; quota via /v1/rate_limit/.
repos.not_when: Need video (v1 has no video); need guaranteed licence; need >200 searches/day anonymous; offline work.
techniques: License filter is mandatory - license=cc0,by,pdm first; for commercial posting use license_type=commercial; never use NC/ND/SA for a published film. Openverse does not verify licences - read the item page.

One search per sound kind - anonymous limit 20 req/min burst, 200/day (secondary sources differ); page_size max 20 anonymous. Search once per cue, pick from the shortlist, do not re-search with rephrasings.
Attribution verbatim - copy each file's attribution field into credits.txt; CC BY is only legal with credit; log CC0/PDM too.
Duration check before download - use the duration field to match the cue length; reject clips too short/long for the shot.
Source filter for reliability - source=freesound,jamendo for SFX/music.
Sound rule - picture must work muted; SFX hit lands 1 frame after its picture event, +3-6 dB over the music bed.
unverified: Rate limit: 20/min + 200/day in one source vs ~100/day in another - not re-tested
Audio count 5.2M vs 800M total is from secondary sources
Registered-tier limits not checked
repos.use_when: Need real, licensed SFX/music/images; no budget for stock.

repos.call_how: pip install librosa; import librosa in a Python script (agent runs it as a measurement tool, output is a timing JSON for the skill's beat_grid).
repos.description: Python library for audio and music analysis.
repos.mechanism: Load audio (librosa.load, default sr 22050), compute STFT/CQT/mel spectrograms, then beat.beat_track, onset.onset_detect, feature.chroma_cqt/mfcc/rms etc. Input: wav/mp3; output: BPM, beat/onset times in seconds, feature matrices.
repos.not_when: Silent film; no audio; need real-time analysis; need synthesis or loudness (librosa is analysis only).
techniques: Beat grid from real audio - tempo, beat_frames = librosa.beat.beat_track(y, sr); beat_times = librosa.frames_to_time(beat_frames, sr); frames-per-beat = fps x 60 / BPM; cut on the beat, change layout on the bar (every 4 beats).

Fallback when beats approx 0 (ambient/synth) - onset_env = librosa.onset.onset_strength(y, sr); onset_tempo = librosa.beat.tempo(onset_envelope=onset_env, sr=sr); sanitise BPM, default 120.0 if all fails.
Onset triggers - onset_detect(y, sr, units='time') gives note-onset times for SFX/cut triggers; backtrack to the onset envelope for accuracy.
Section segmentation - chroma_cqt + melspectrogram + rms (RMS weighted 5x), beat-sync with librosa.util.sync, cluster into intro/verse/chorus/drop/outro; pacing follows sections, not a flat grid.
Harmonic-percussive separation + YIN pitch (piptrack) - drive motion from drums vs melody separately, not from a single loudness curve.
Keep hop_length (default 512) consistent, or frames_to_time drifts.

API signatures not checked against a pinned version
Tempo accuracy on non-music audio not tested
repos.use_when: Music-driven film; beat grid must come from the actual track, not a guessed BPM.

repos.call_how: CLI whisperx audio.wav --model large-v2 --language ja --diarize --highlight_words True; Python load_model -> transcribe -> load_align_model -> align -> assign_word_speakers.
repos.description: Fast ASR (70x realtime, large-v2) with word-level timestamps and speaker diarization.
repos.mechanism: VAD pre-processing -> batched faster-whisper transcription -> wav2vec2 forced alignment (phoneme-level) -> pyannote diarization. Input: audio file; output: segments with per-word start/end, speaker IDs, SRT.
repos.not_when: No speech; music-only; overlapping speech; words with no characters in the alignment dictionary (e.g. '2014.', '£13.60') get no timing (README limitation).
techniques: Word-level, never line-level - never fake word timing by splitting a line evenly over its duration; drift is instantly visible. Normalise all sources to {text, startMs, endMs}[].
VAD first - reduces hallucination and enables batching with no WER degradation (per README).
Language-specific alignment - --language <code> auto-picks the alignment model; defaults for en/fr/de/es/it via torchaudio, others via Hugging Face; a wrong-language model gives wrong word times.
Context flags - --interleaved_context / condition_on_previous_context for punctuation and proper nouns on long audio.
Diarization - --diarize --min_speakers N --max_speakers N, HF read token required; labels are speaker IDs, not names; diarization is 'far from perfect' (README).

Compute trade-offs - large-v2 <8 GB GPU at beam_size=5; reduce batch_size (default 16) if low on memory; --compute_type int8 --device cpu for CPU/Mac; Numba (whisperx[fast]) accelerates alignment 30-100x.
Caption paging - group 4-6 words/page or createTikTokStyleCaptions(combineTokensWithinMilliseconds: 1200); active word highlighted, spring pop scale 0.6->1, active 1->1.1.
unverified: Did not run; '70x realtime' and '<8 GB' are README claims

repos.use_when: Narration/voiceover, captions, lip-sync or word-synced motion.

repos.call_how: npx remotion skills add, or npx skills add remotion-dev/skills, or gh skill install remotion-dev/skills; then /remotion-captions, /remotion-markup, etc. in Claude Code / Codex / Cursor.
repos.description: Agent Skills for Remotion - 12 skills defining best practices for AI agents building video in Remotion.
repos.mechanism: A router skill (remotion-best-practices) plus per-task skills (create, markup, studio, render, maps, captions, saas, interactivity, docs, license, upgrade, multimedia), each a SKILL.md (+ REFERENCE.md); installed into a Remotion project and invoked as /remotion-* commands.
repos.not_when: Single-HTML Canvas2D route, Blender, Manim, or any non-React stack; no Node/React available.
techniques: Router + preserve user changes - best-practices skill routes to the right sub-skill; if the user edited code outside the conversation, do not overwrite it, assume intentional or ask.

Pure function of frame - useCurrentFrame() is the only clock; no Date.now, Math.random, timers, or accumulated state; CSS transitions/animations forbidden (they will not render). This is the React form of renderAt(t).
Prefer interpolate() over spring() unless physics is requested; clamp both sides; Easing.out for entrances, Easing.in for exits; e.g. Easing.bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) over ~45f for a crisp UI entrance.

Caption type + TikTok paging - Caption {text, startMs, endMs, timestampMs, confidence, pageBreakAfter?}; createTikTokStyleCaptions({captions, combineTokensWithinMilliseconds: 1200}); page in a <Sequence>; active token when token.fromMs <= timeMs < token.toMs; word spring damping 10-15, mass 0.5-0.8.
Async discipline - delayRender() / continueRender() / cancelRender(err) for fonts, captions, Lottie; failure must fail the render, not silently render a placeholder.
Preview gate - open Remotion Studio after an edit so the user can preview and steer; render skill for stills/video.

repos.call_how: CLI ffmpeg / ffprobe; in the skill, wrap as stdlib Python subprocess with measured outputs recorded, never as an imported library.
repos.description: Mirror of https://git.ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg.git - libraries and tools to process audio, video, subtitles and metadata.
repos.mechanism: ffmpeg CLI (transcode/filter/mux) + ffprobe (inspect) + ffplay; libraries libavcodec/format/util/filter/device, libswresample, libswscale. Input: PNG frame sequences / audio / video; output: encoded MP4/MOV/WebM/GIF + loudness/QC measurements.
repos.not_when: Drawing/animating (it is not a renderer); deterministic frame generation (that is renderAt(t)); if GPL-licensed components in a given build matter - check the build configuration.
techniques: Encode spec - ffmpeg -framerate 30 -i frames/%04d.png -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 16-18 -movflags +faststart out.mp4; PNG frames only, never JPEG; set colour tags in the filter chain (setparams=...bt709).

Two-pass loudness - measure first: loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1:LRA=11:print_format=json -f null -; apply measured values second pass; force -ar 48000; verify on the encoded file with ebur128=peak=true (AAC changes peaks - a file held at -1.0 dBTP in WAV can come back at -0.9 dBTP). Target -14 LUFS, true peak <= -1 dBTP.

QC on the encoded file, not the renderer - freezedetect (warn frozen >=1s outside declared holds), blackdetect=d=0.1:pix_th=0.10 (warn black >=0.1s), silencedetect, signalstats YDIF; warn, do not fail, on dark-interface / slow-camera false positives.
Contact sheet + phone test - fps=2,scale=270:-1,tile=6x5 contact sheet; scale=360:-1 phone test; stream_loop 2 loop-seam check.
GIF export - fps=25,scale=1200:-1,palettegen/paletteuse, <=15 MB, <=350 frames; 25 fps is exact in GIF hundredths, 24 fps runs ~4% fast.
Probe first - ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams INPUT before deciding; never trust renderer-internal numbers.

GPL/LGPL split depends on build config, not checked
GitHub PRs are ignored upstream - patches go to ffmpeg-devel
